name: Wyrmfire
summary: Chapter 4 of The Seven Teeth of Vashkul. The Ember Tooth lodged in Pyrraxis’s old wound is the Choir’s last weapon: its singers drive the maddened red dragon against Highcrown while a Choir coup seizes the palace. The hero must reach Millbrook before the dragon does, gather the realm at a war council in Dawnspire Keep, climb Emberpeak to silence the dragon-callers, slay, free or bargain with Pyrraxis in her lair, and break the coup in the burning capital, where the sick Queen has one last chance.

chapters.name: Wyrmfire
chapters.summary: The dragon Pyrraxis burns her way toward Highcrown while the Choir seizes the palace. Gather the realm, face the dragon, save the capital.

scenes.name: The Ashfall Road
scenes.seed: The Silverrun road north of Brightwater is choked with refugees from burned farms: carts piled with bedding, children carrying hens, a priest of Solenne leading a blind ox. Smoke hangs over the southern hills. On the ridge above, figures in red-daubed robes sing and wave torches, herding the crowd toward the burning fields instead of the river bridge.

variants.seed: A Crown patrol sits its horses at the bridge. The sergeant has your face on a wanted poster, and his riders will not lift a hand to help you.
A Crown patrol holds the bridge, uncertain, waiting for someone to tell it what to do.
The patrol riders wear black ribbons: word has spread that the Queen lies humming in her sickbed.
Someone has chalked "THE ALMONER LIED" on the milestone, over an older Almonry relief notice.
Master Moll's empty barges are specks far down the river.
Master Moll glares at you from the stern of her barge, loaded to the gunwales with refugees.

onEnter.text: A shadow crosses the sun. High above the smoke, a vast red shape wheels once over the valley and turns toward Highcrown: Pyrraxis, awake and hungry. Millbrook lies squarely in her path, a day to the south.

actions.label: Stand your ground as the dragon passes

success.text: You hold your ground and watch her go. The refugees nearest you stop screaming, because you have not.

failure.text: Your legs lock and your hands shake until the shadow has passed. For a long moment you are no braver than the crowd.

actions.label: Calm the panicking crowd

success.text: Your voice carries over the panic. The crowd stops pushing and starts listening.

failure.text: Nobody can hear you over the screaming. The crowd tramples the ditch-reeds flat.

actions.label: Lead the refugees down to the river

advantageIf.source: The crowd is listening to you

success.text: You find the old towpath below the ridge and lead the refugees down to the river, out of the singers’ sight.

failure.text: The towpath is washed out. You bring the crowd back up the bank, closer to the singers than before.

actions.label: Pay the barge-masters to carry the refugees downriver (50 gp)

outcome.text: Master Moll takes your fifty gold and packs the refugees onto her grain barges, three to a sack, and casts off for the north bank.

actions.label: Call on the Crown patrol to ride with you

outcome.text: The patrol sergeant salutes, relieved to have orders, and forms his riders up behind you.

actions.label: Charge the ember-singers on the ridge

outcome.text: You charge the ridge. The ember-singers break off their hymn, and fire answers them from the burning fields.

actions.label: Charge the ember-singers with the Crown patrol

outcome.text: You charge the ridge with the Crown riders at your back. The ember-singers call fire out of the burning fields to meet you.

actions.label: Leave the refugees and ride on

outcome.text: You leave the refugees to find their own way and ride on. Behind you the singing does not stop.

exits.label: Ride south to Millbrook, in the dragon’s path
Ride for Dawnspire Keep and the war council

scenes.revisitSeed: The Ashfall road again, ash drifting over the ditches and the river beyond.

scenes.name: Millbrook Remembers
scenes.seed: Millbrook lies squarely in the dragon’s path: a green valley of barley and hedges below the barrow hill, where your road began.

variants.seed: Reeve Tamsin has the whole village out. Men with pitchforks muster on the green, women wet down the thatch, and a line of hay wagons stands across the southern lane as a firebreak.
The village is quiet in the wrong way. The doors are painted with seven-tooth sigils, and villagers stand in the lane with their eyes shut, humming the Choir’s hymn.
Half the village is loading carts to flee north, and the other half is arguing on the green about whether to stay.
You are too late. Millbrook is ash: the mill is a black stump, the Plough tavern a heap of smoking timbers, and the barley is burned to the foot of the barrow hill.
Pip Hallard, the boy you carried out of the barrow, rides in on a lathered pony in a Dawn Lance page’s tabard, waving a sealed letter.
Widow Marrow waits at her shop door, wearing the ring you brought back and holding something wrapped in oilcloth.
On the barrow hill, the shrine you rekindled still burns with a small green flame.
A pale ring of green Thaloren fire circles the village.
The southern lane is a strip of wet mud and torn-down sheds: a firebreak.
The children and the old folk are gone north. The village feels very quiet without them.
Two knights of the Dawn Lance sit their horses on the green, sent by Thane.

actions.label: Search the ashes of the village

outcome.text: In the ashes of the Plough you find the Reeve’s militia horn, cracked by the heat. Whoever lived has fled north. Whoever stayed is under the rubble.

actions.label: Wake the barrow’s old wards from the rekindled shrine

outcome.text: The shrine you rekindled answers at a word. Its Thaloren wards wake and spread a pale ring of green fire around the village; dragonfire will not catch inside it.

actions.label: Remember how the barrow’s old wards were lit

success.text: You remember the barrow’s carvings: Thaloren wards against fire. Lit again at the old stones, they spread a pale green ring around the village; dragonfire will not catch inside it.

failure.text: The barrow’s carvings mean nothing to you. The stones stay cold.

actions.label: Visit Widow Marrow

outcome.text: "He’d want it used on someone brave," says Widow Marrow, and gives you her late husband’s two potions of heroism.

actions.label: Take Pip’s letter

outcome.text: Pip salutes badly and hands you Lord-Commander Thane’s letter: the Dawn Lance musters at Dawnspire Keep, and asks for you by name. "I’ll ride ahead and tell them you’re coming," says Pip.

actions.label: Take command of Reeve Tamsin’s militia

outcome.text: Reeve Tamsin grips your arm. "You brought our people home from that barrow. Millbrook stands with you." The militia forms up behind the hay wagons.

actions.label: Talk the frightened villagers into standing and fighting

advantageIf.source: The families you brought home from the barrow speak for you
You know what they are really afraid of
Reeve Tamsin goes door to door beside you

success.text: You stand on a cart and remind them what you pulled out of the barrow. One by one, the carts are unloaded. Millbrook will fight.

failure.text: The Reeve shakes his head. The families load their carts and go north. You will hold the lane without them.

disadvantageIf.source: Reeve Tamsin has told the village to ignore you

actions.label: Hold the southern lane with the militia

outcome.text: Two hell hounds come howling up the southern lane ahead of the smoke. The militia levels its pitchforks behind the hay wagons.

actions.label: Hold the southern lane inside the wards

outcome.text: Two hell hounds come howling up the southern lane. Their fire gutters out against the green ward-light.

actions.label: Hold the southern lane alone

outcome.text: Two hell hounds come howling up the southern lane and breathe fire into the thatch around you.

actions.label: Break the Choir’s hold on three of the humming villagers

advantageIf.source: You know the voice they are hearing, and how to argue with it
You know whose names to call, and in what order
Reeve Tamsin calls the names beside you

success.text: Three villagers stop humming at once and blink at you like sleepers woken. They sit down in the lane and weep.

failure.text: They keep humming. The song has these three too deep.

disadvantageIf.source: Reeve Tamsin has turned his back on you

actions.label: Subdue the converted villagers and their fanatic

outcome.text: The Choir’s fanatic lifts his torch, and six humming villagers come at you with flails and sickles, the hell hounds at their heels. You must not kill them.

actions.label: Subdue the last humming villagers and their fanatic

outcome.text: The fanatic screams at the three you freed, and the three still humming come at you with sickles. You must not kill them.

actions.label: Take down the fanatic and his hounds

outcome.text: With his flock awake, the fanatic has only his hell hounds left. He looses them at you.

exits.label: Ride back up the Ashfall road

revisitSeed: Millbrook again: the mill, the green, the smell of smoke on the wind.
Back in Millbrook, where every face turns to see who has come up the lane.

scenes.name: The Muster at Dawnspire
scenes.seed: Dawnspire Keep has lit every brazier on its walls. Banners you never expected to see together hang in its great hall, and Lord-Commander Aldric Thane stands at a war table marked with Emberpeak, Highcrown and the road between. There are six empty chairs around it.

variants.seed: Dawnbreaker hangs above the war table, polished for battle.
The knights keep glancing at Dawnbreaker on your back.
Dawnbreaker’s rack is still empty.
Thane has hidden your wanted poster under a map, but the royal envoy has seen it and will not sit near you.
The royal envoy wears black: the Queen still hums in her sickbed in Highcrown.
Everyone here knows the Royal Almoner is the Cantor. The anger in the hall is a living thing.
Pip runs messages between the delegations, breathless and proud.
Ser Corwin stands at your shoulder, and the knights at the table cannot decide whether to salute him.
Millbrook's children play in the keep's yard, underfoot and delighted.
Chamberlain Hale nods to you stiffly. The wanted posters have come down from the gate.
Corwin has the Order's badge in his pocket, not on his cloak.

onEnter.text: Thane meets you at the gate. "The dragon is flying, the Choir is singing, and I have six empty chairs at my war table. Let us see who comes."

actions.label: Ask the Dawn Lance to ride

outcome.text: Thane lays his gauntlet on the table. "The Dawn Lance rides. My knights will be at Highcrown when the Choir shows its face."

actions.label: Persuade Thane’s doubtful captains to ride

advantageIf.source: Pip carries your messages between the delegations
Ser Corwin speaks for you
The captains cheered your speech

success.text: The captains argue, then look to Thane. He nods once. The Dawn Lance will ride with you.

failure.text: Thane’s captains will not ride under a stranger’s banner. The Order will hold Dawnspire and nothing more.

disadvantageIf.source: The captains were not impressed by your speech

actions.label: Ask the royal envoy for the royal guard

outcome.text: Chamberlain Hale signs the order with a shaking hand: the royal guard will fight for the palace at your side.

actions.label: Tell Chamberlain Hale what you know about the Almoner

advantageIf.source: Pip carries your messages between the delegations
Chamberlain Hale speaks for you
Chamberlain Hale dares not refuse you

success.text: Hale goes grey as you speak, then signs the order. "If you are wrong, we are all traitors. If you are right, we are all fools." The royal guard will fight at your side.

failure.text: Hale will not hear a word against the Almoner without proof. The royal guard stays in its barracks.

actions.label: Ask Guildmistress Ashgrove for the Consortium’s ballistae

outcome.text: Guildmistress Ashgrove’s clerks have already priced the war. "Six ballistae and their crews, at the Consortium’s expense. The Almonry’s frozen accounts will pay for them."

actions.label: Talk Guildmistress Ashgrove round

advantageIf.source: Pip carries your messages between the delegations
You know the Consortium fears a dead debtor
Ashgrove is afraid of what the Choir will do

success.text: Ashgrove sighs and signs. "A dragon is bad for business. Six ballistae, and the Crown owes us for every bolt."

failure.text: Ashgrove folds her ledger. "The Consortium does not forget who cost it money." Her ballistae stay in Deepanvil.

disadvantageIf.source: Ashgrove has not forgiven your threat

actions.label: Call in Saltwind’s promise of gunpowder

outcome.text: Factor Ashcombe promises Saltwind gunpowder and gun crews, hauled up the river on Company barges.

actions.label: Call in Governor Pell’s debt: all the gunpowder in Port Sorrel

outcome.text: Governor Pell, anxious to stay your friend, empties Port Sorrel’s magazines: twice the gunpowder Factor Ashcombe promised.

actions.label: Send for Captain Quint’s fire-ships

outcome.text: Marisol Quint grins. "Fire-ships up the Silverrun? The Brotherhood has waited a hundred years to sail into Highcrown with the Crown’s blessing."

actions.label: Ask Oswin Tull for Gullhaven’s fire-barges

advantageIf.source: Pip carries your messages between the delegations

success.text: Tull scratches his beard. "Gullhaven owes you its freedom. You’ll have your fire-barges, and my best gunners."

failure.text: Tull shakes his head. "Gullhaven has one fleet and a hundred enemies. I cannot send it upriver."

actions.label: Seat Millbrook’s militia at the table

outcome.text: Reeve Tamsin’s riders arrive with hay wagons and wet sacking. Millbrook’s firebreak crews will march with you to Highcrown.

actions.label: Hire the Deepanvil mercenaries with the Brass Parrot’s treasure

outcome.text: You pay the Deepanvil mercenaries in pirate gold. Their captain bites a coin, grins, and swears the company to your banner until Highcrown is taken.

actions.label: Hire the Deepanvil mercenaries (1,500 gp)

outcome.text: You count out fifteen hundred gold. The Deepanvil company swears to your banner until Highcrown is taken.

actions.label: Hire the Deepanvil mercenaries on the Crown's draft

outcome.text: The Deepanvil captain reads Hale's draft twice, bites the seal, and swears the company to your banner until Highcrown is taken.

actions.label: Buy a fire-resistance tonic from the Keep’s quartermaster (300 gp)

outcome.text: The quartermaster sells you a flask of fire-resistance tonic brewed by the Order’s chaplains for the last assault on Emberpeak, twenty-three years ago.

actions.label: Close the war council and ride for Emberpeak at dawn

outcome.text: Thane rolls up the maps. "It is enough, or it will have to be. We ride for Emberpeak at dawn."

exits.label: Ride back to the Ashfall road

scenes.revisitSeed: Dawnspire Keep again, loud with smiths and horses and the arguments of the war council.

scenes.name: The Emberpeak Ascent
scenes.seed: Emberpeak’s slopes are black glass and grey ash. Every few hundred yards the path passes the melted armor of a failed hero, fused into the rock where they fell. Far above, a sound rises and falls on the hot wind: dozens of voices singing to the mountain.

variants.seed: Among the voices you hear one you know: Vosk the Hollow, leading the hymn.
The hymn is led by a Choir cantor-mage whose voice cracks on the high notes.
Below you, Ironvault crews drag six ballistae up the lower slope, cursing the ash.
Nobody up here cares about wanted posters.

actions.label: Climb the glassy lower slopes

success.text: You find the old dwarf-cut steps under the ash and climb steadily.

failure.text: A ledge of glass gives way under you. You slide thirty feet down the slope before you catch a spur of rock, and climb again, bleeding.

actions.label: Drink the fire-resistance tonic before the lava fields

outcome.text: You drink the tonic. The heat still hurts, but it no longer cooks you.

actions.label: Cross the lava fields in the killing heat

success.text: You cross the lava fields in an hour of shimmering heat, dizzy but whole.

failure.text: The heat hammers you for an hour. By the end you are staggering, and your lips are cracked and bleeding.

actions.label: Walk the lava fields under the tonic’s protection

outcome.text: Warded against fire, you walk the lava fields untouched while the air shimmers around you.

actions.label: Force a way through the lava tubes

outcome.text: The lava tubes are the only way to the summit. In the red dark ahead, something made of fire uncoils.

actions.label: Creep up on the singers’ crater unseen

success.text: You reach the lip of the singers’ crater unseen. Below, a ring of cultists sings around a black stone pulsing with red light: the song-stone that carries their hymn to the Ember Tooth.

failure.text: Scree clatters under your boots. A cultist looks up and shrieks, and the hymn becomes a war-cry.

actions.label: Unpick the song-stone’s enchantment

success.text: You find the thread of the song in the stone and pull it loose. The stone goes quiet, whole and harmless, and far above you the dragon’s roar changes.

failure.text: The enchantment is Vosk’s work, and it slides away from your understanding.

advantageIf.source: Vosk told you which note silences it

actions.label: Smash the song-stone

outcome.text: You bring the stone down on the rocks. It shatters with a sound like a bell cracking, and the hymn dies in every throat at once.

actions.label: Storm the dragon-callers’ camp

outcome.text: You come down into the crater. The dragon-callers break their circle and draw knives, and their mage lifts a hand full of fire.

actions.label: Signal the ballistae and storm the camp

outcome.text: You wave the signal flag. The Ironvault ballistae open up from the lower slope; a bolt skewers one fanatic and flattens the camp’s palisade before you charge.

actions.label: Take Vosk alive

outcome.text: Vosk surrenders with ash in his beard. "You cannot stop the song," he says, "you can only choose where you stand when it ends." You bind his hands and send him down the mountain with a Dawn Lance escort.

actions.label: Finish Vosk

outcome.text: Vosk the Hollow dies on the mountain he woke. His last breath is a note of the hymn.

exits.label: Retreat down the mountain to Dawnspire

scenes.revisitSeed: The glassy slopes of Emberpeak again, the summit smoking above you.

scenes.name: The Hoard of Pyrraxis
scenes.seed: The heart of Emberpeak is a cavern the size of a cathedral, floored with melted gold and coin. Pyrraxis lies coiled on her hoard: vast, scarred, one wing ragged. In the old wound on her breast a tooth-shaped shard glows like a coal, and every time it pulses she snarls with hunger. On a ledge above, her brood-guardian paces, a younger red dragon with smoke curling from its jaws.

variants.seed: Without the Choir’s song, her eyes are clearer. She is watching you, not the dark.
The Choir’s hymn still echoes up the lava tubes, and every note makes her claws flex.
Dawnbreaker hums in your hands. She knows it: it is the lance that wounded her.
Thane’s knights have followed you up the tubes; the foremost carries Dawnbreaker couched like a spear.
Ser Corwin is white to the lips, but he has not stepped back.
Her nostrils flare. She can smell the Teeth you carry.
Your artillery crews have hauled their engines to the crater rim above the lair.
The cavern is empty now but for the gold.

actions.label: Signal the artillery on the rim to drive off the brood-guardian

outcome.text: You signal the rim. Ballista bolts and powder-kegs slam into the ledge until the brood-guardian flees shrieking into the smoke.

actions.label: Fight the brood-guardian

outcome.text: The brood-guardian drops from its ledge in a storm of wings and fire.

actions.label: Attack Pyrraxis

outcome.text: Pyrraxis uncoils from her hoard. Molten gold runs off her scales like water.

actions.label: Attack Pyrraxis with Thane’s knights and Dawnbreaker

outcome.text: The knights of the Dawn Lance level their spears, Dawnbreaker at their point. Pyrraxis remembers that lance, and screams.

actions.label: Cut the Ember Tooth out of the old wound (Medicine)

advantageIf.source: Without the Choir’s song, she holds still for you
Nettle steadies your hands
Thane showed you where the old wound lies

success.text: The Ember Tooth shifts in the wound. Pyrraxis hisses, and her claw rakes past you.

failure.text: The Tooth slips deeper. Pyrraxis roars and lashes out with a claw.

actions.label: Sing against the Choir’s hunger in the Tooth (Religion)

advantageIf.source: Without the Choir’s song, she holds still for you
Aurek knows the Choir’s hymn backwards
The dragon under the hunger is fighting with you

success.text: The Ember Tooth shifts in the wound. Pyrraxis hisses, and her claw rakes past you.

failure.text: The Tooth slips deeper. Pyrraxis roars and lashes out with a claw.

actions.label: Wrench the Ember Tooth free (Athletics)

advantageIf.source: Without the Choir’s song, she holds still for you
Ser Corwin braces the wound with his shield
Thane showed you where the old wound lies
She holds still under Dawnbreaker's point

success.text: The Ember Tooth shifts in the wound. Pyrraxis hisses, and her claw rakes past you.

failure.text: The Tooth slips deeper. Pyrraxis roars and lashes out with a claw.

actions.label: Offer Pyrraxis a Tooth for the Ember Tooth

advantageIf.source: She hungers for the Teeth you carry
The dragon under the hunger wants the song to stop
She enjoyed your manners

success.text: She lowers her head until her eye is level with you, bigger than a cart-wheel. "One tooth for another, little thief. Choose."

failure.text: She laughs, and the laugh is fire. "You would haggle with me in my own house?"

disadvantageIf.source: You threatened her with the lance

actions.label: Give her the Tooth of Want

outcome.text: She takes the Tooth of Want delicately in her teeth, then tears the Ember Tooth from her own breast and spits it at your feet, smoking. With one beat of her ragged wings she is gone toward the Gloamfen, to feed. The Choir will be waiting for her there.

actions.label: Give her the Drowned Tooth

outcome.text: She takes the Drowned Tooth delicately in her teeth, then tears the Ember Tooth from her own breast and spits it at your feet, smoking. With one beat of her ragged wings she is gone toward the Gloamfen, to feed. The Choir will be waiting for her there.

actions.label: Give her the Briar Tooth

outcome.text: She takes the Briar Tooth delicately in her teeth, then tears the Ember Tooth from her own breast and spits it at your feet, smoking. With one beat of her ragged wings she is gone toward the Gloamfen, to feed. The Choir will be waiting for her there.

actions.label: Give her the Brass Tooth

outcome.text: She takes the Brass Tooth delicately in her teeth, then tears the Ember Tooth from her own breast and spits it at your feet, smoking. With one beat of her ragged wings she is gone toward the Gloamfen, to feed. The Choir will be waiting for her there.

actions.label: Give her the Singing Tooth

outcome.text: She takes the Singing Tooth delicately in her teeth, then tears the Ember Tooth from her own breast and spits it at your feet, smoking. With one beat of her ragged wings she is gone toward the Gloamfen, to feed. The Choir will be waiting for her there.

actions.label: Give her the Sky Tooth

outcome.text: She takes the Sky Tooth delicately in her teeth, then tears the Ember Tooth from her own breast and spits it at your feet, smoking. With one beat of her ragged wings she is gone toward the Gloamfen, to feed. The Choir will be waiting for her there.

actions.label: Retreat from the lair

outcome.text: You back out of the cavern. Behind you Pyrraxis rises roaring from her hoard, and the Choir’s hymn swells to meet her. She will burn Highcrown now, and when she is done the singers will take the Ember Tooth.

actions.label: Take what you can carry of the hoard

outcome.text: You fill every pack you have with the dragon’s gold. Among it you find a sword whose blade kindles at a word and a plain red-gold ring that is cool to the touch.

scenes.name: Highcrown Burning
scenes.seed: Highcrown is burning from the inside. Choir banners hang from the palace walls, converted nobles and dead things hold the upper gates, and the temple bells are ringing backwards. Smoke pours up the tiers from the lower city.

variants.seed: And above it all, Pyrraxis: she circles the tiers, and wherever her shadow falls the streets go up in flame.
Word of Pyrraxis’s death has run ahead of you. The defenders at the Queen’s Gate cheer when they see you.
The sky above the city is empty of dragons. Somewhere far to the east, Pyrraxis is flying home.
The sky above the city is empty of dragons. You know where Pyrraxis has gone, and who is waiting for her there.
The Ember Tooth burns in your pack, and the Choir’s singers on the walls all turn toward it at once.
The Choir holds Queen Isolde in her own throne hall, sick and humming, a hostage on her dais.
Queen Isolde is a prisoner in her own throne hall, and the Choir’s cantors are singing at her to make her kneel.
Your face is on the wanted posters by the gate. The city watch does not know whether to arrest you or cheer.
Millbrook’s firebreak crews are already tearing down burning sheds and wetting the thatch in the lanes.
Red Gull fire-ships burn the Choir’s barges on the Silverrun below the walls.
Gun crews from the isles are dragging cannon up the lower tiers.
There is so much Saltwind powder on the quay that nobody dares light a pipe.
The knights of the Dawn Lance form up at the Queen’s Gate.
The royal guard holds the gatehouse, waiting for you to lead them in.
The Deepanvil mercenaries are sharpening axes in the shadow of the gate.
Ser Corwin rides with the Dawn Lance, and salutes you once across the smoke.
The crowds know who did this. "The Almoner!" they shout, and spit on the Almonry’s gilded doors.
On the left of the knights' line you see Corwin's banner, as he promised.
Harrow Vey's ship is a smudge on the river, heading for the sea.

actions.label: Force a way up the burning Street of Lamps

success.text: You haul a burning cart out of the way and lead the defenders up the Street of Lamps.

failure.text: A burning roof collapses as you pass under it. You get through, scorched.

actions.label: Clear the burning Tanners’ Stair

success.text: You kick through a smouldering barricade and the Tanners’ Stair is open to the palace.

failure.text: The Tanners’ Stair is an oven. You get through, but not unhurt.

actions.label: Storm the palace court

outcome.text: Harrow Vey holds the palace court with Choir pirates. "Small world," he calls, and draws.

actions.label: Take Harrow Vey alive

outcome.text: Harrow Vey spits blood and laughs. "Hang me in the isles, at least. I want to hear the gulls." The royal guard drags him away.

actions.label: Finish Harrow Vey

outcome.text: Harrow Vey dies on the palace flagstones, a long way from the sea.

actions.label: Storm the grand stair

outcome.text: Vosk the Hollow waits at the top of the grand stair with his last fanatics. "Again?" he says wearily, and the air fills with fire.

actions.label: Take Vosk alive

outcome.text: Vosk lets his hands fall. "Take me, then. She has what she needs from me." The guards chain him.

actions.label: Finish Vosk

outcome.text: Vosk the Hollow dies on the grand stair, and his notes burn with him.

actions.label: Storm the throne hall with the Dawn Lance

outcome.text: The knights of the Dawn Lance crash through the throne-hall doors behind you.

actions.label: Storm the throne hall with the royal guard

outcome.text: The royal guard follows you into the throne hall, shouting the Queen’s name.

actions.label: Storm the throne hall with the Deepanvil mercenaries

outcome.text: The Deepanvil company goes through the throne-hall doors axes first.

actions.label: Storm the throne hall

outcome.text: You kick open the throne-hall doors. A wight in a noble’s coat sits on the Queen’s throne, and the dead rise from the pews to meet you.

actions.label: Give the Queen the fen cure

outcome.text: Bell-ash, bitterroot and a Briarkin chant: you have seen this cure work before. By dawn the Queen stops humming and asks for water.

actions.label: Fight for the Queen’s life

advantageIf.source: Nettle has fought the Sickness in Hollowmere

success.text: You work through the night, bleeding the spores out of her one breath at a time. At dawn, Isolde stops humming and opens her eyes.

failure.text: You do everything you know. Near dawn, Queen Isolde stops humming, and then stops breathing.

actions.label: Ask Isolde to write to her godmother

outcome.text: Isolde writes for a long time. When she seals the letter her hands are steady. "Give her this, if you find her. Tell her I remember the lullabies too."

actions.label: Kneel for the Queen’s pardon

outcome.text: Isolde touches your shoulder with her father’s sword. "Whatever you were accused of, you are pardoned for it, by the Crown and by me."

actions.label: Leave the burning city with the survivors
Stand among the ashes of the upper tiers
Stand beside the Queen as the fires go out
Stand vigil over the Queen’s body

npcs.name: Master Ida Moll
npcs.personality: A broad, sunburned barge-master of Brightwater who hates waste, debt and cultists, in that order. Generous once she has decided you are worth it.
secrets: Her grain barges carried Almonry relief sacks last spring, and she has been sick with worry ever since.
npcs.voice: Loud river-town bellow, counts everything out loud, calls everyone "duck".

conversations.label: Talk to Master Moll about her barges

success.text: Moll snorts. "Twenty, and you carry the first sack yourself." She packs the refugees onto her grain barges and casts off for the north bank.

failure.text: "Fifty," says Moll, "or swim."

success.text: Moll spits over the side. The singers burned two of her barges at Brightwater. "When you go up that ridge," she says, "my bargemen will be in the reeds with poles and buckets, drawing off those little fire-imps."

npcs.name: Reeve Hollis Tamsin
npcs.personality: Tired, honest and proud, and ashamed he could not protect his village the first time. He remembers exactly what the hero did at the barrow.
secrets: He buried two militia men after the barrow and never told their widows how they died.
npcs.voice: Slow farmer’s drawl; long pauses before anything important.

conversations.label: Talk to Reeve Tamsin about the defence

nodes.text: Reeve Tamsin looks older than when you last saw him. "The dragon, the Choir, both at once. Tell me what to do, and I will try to do it."

options.label: "Wet the thatch and pull down the sheds on the southern lane. A firebreak." (Survival DC 13)

success.text: Tamsin sets every bucket in Millbrook to work. By noon the southern lane is a strip of wet mud and torn-down sheds. Whatever comes up it will have less to burn, and one less way in.

failure.text: You pick the wrong lane to clear. By the time you notice, half the buckets are empty.

options.label: "What are they really afraid of, Reeve?" (Insight DC 14)

success.text: Tamsin rubs his face. "Not the dragon. Being left behind again, like the night the Choir took our children and nobody came." Now you know what to say to them.

failure.text: "Dragons," says Tamsin flatly. "What else?"

options.label: "Who started the humming? Who did the Choir reach first?" (Insight DC 14)

success.text: Tamsin will not look at you, but he answers. The miller's wife heard the song first, then her neighbours, house by house. You know now whose names to call, and in what order.

failure.text: Tamsin only shakes his head and walks away down the lane.

success.text: The words hit Tamsin like a slap. He straightens, takes up his old sword and goes from door to door beside you, shouting names.

failure.text: Tamsin's face closes like a door. "Get out of my village," he says, loud enough for the lane to hear.

npcs.name: Widow Marrow
npcs.personality: Millbrook’s sharp-tongued shopkeeper, practical to the bone, soft only about her late husband.
secrets: Her husband marched with the Dawn Lance in the Ashfall Winter and came home with two potions he swore never to drink.
npcs.voice: Brisk and dry, sniffs before she says anything kind.

npcs.name: Pip Hallard
npcs.personality: The miller's son from Millbrook, rescued from the barrow, now a page of the Dawn Lance and utterly devoted to the hero.
npcs.voice: Breathless and eager; calls the hero "my lord" or "my lady" whatever they say.

npcs.personality: A scarred veteran of the Ashfall Winter who lost his lance and half his knights. Honourable to a fault and slow to forgive.

secrets: Has warned the Queen twice that the Almonry spends too freely, and been laughed at.

npcs.name: Guildmistress Brunhild Ashgrove
npcs.personality: A shrewd dwarf who measures every favor in coin and never forgets a debt. Honest, but never generous.
secrets: The Almonry's loans frighten her: no charity borrows like that.

npcs.name: Factor Wendel Ashcombe
npcs.personality: A Saltwind agent in a fisherman’s smock, patient and polite, who has never once enjoyed himself.
secrets: Has orders to find Gullhaven’s weak points before the squadron sails.
npcs.voice: Soft, clipped, clerkish; speaks in terms and conditions.

npcs.name: Captain Marisol "Two-Hats" Quint
npcs.personality: A dashing half-elf captain who wears two hats at once, one for each fortune won and lost. Never breaks a promise, though she often bends one.
secrets: Wants the Brass Parrot treasure for the islands, not herself.
Rook is her cousin-in-law and her soft spot.
npcs.voice: Warm, loud, rolling laugh; swaps her hats when she changes her mind.

npcs.name: Harbormaster Oswin Tull
npcs.personality: A round, cheerful gnome who knows every tide and every rumor, and plays both sides until he has to choose.
secrets: Sold Harrow Vey a reef chart last month, a slightly wrong one.
npcs.voice: Bubbly and fast, full of nautical asides; taps his nose when he lies.

npcs.name: Vosk the Hollow
npcs.personality: A renegade Veyran scholar and the Choir's archivist-mage, eyes sewn shut, courteous and utterly without pity.
secrets: Carries letters from the Cantor in Seraphine's own hand.
npcs.voice: Dry and scholarly; hums the Choir's tune between sentences.

npcs.name: Captain Harrow Vey
npcs.personality: The Choir’s smuggler-captain: charming, handsome, utterly without loyalty to anything but the Choir’s promise of a full belly.
secrets: Grew up starving on a Brinescatter rock; the Choir fed him first.
Answers to someone he calls "the Cantor".
npcs.voice: Honeyed baritone; calls everyone "darling"; never stops smiling.

conversations.label: Call out to Harrow Vey across the court

nodes.text: Harrow Vey leans on the palace fountain with his pirates around him. "Small world. Come to talk, or come to die?"

options.label: "The Choir eats its own last, Vey. Is that the deal you want?" (Persuasion DC 16)

advantageIf.source: Rook knows Vey from the Isles, and says so

success.text: Vey looks at the smoke over the upper tiers for a long moment. "The throne hall. The dead are in the pews, and there is a ghast behind the dais curtain. Mind it." He whistles his pirates off the court and walks out of the city.

failure.text: "Nice try," says Vey, and draws.

options.label: Toss him a heavy purse: "Sail away, captain." (500 gp)

outcome.text: Vey weighs the purse, grins, and bows. "Always a pleasure doing business." He and his pirates melt into the smoke.

options.label: Shout to his crew: "Your captain's already bought his passage out. Did he buy yours?" (Intimidation DC 15)

success.text: Half of Vey's pirates look at each other, and then at the gate, and run for it. Vey swears and draws on you with the rest.

failure.text: The pirates laugh, and Vey draws.

options.label: "Enough talk."

nodes.text: The court is empty but for the smoke.
Steel rings across the palace court.

npcs.name: Ser Corwin Ashvale
npcs.personality: Your former companion, back in the Dawn Lance’s ranks. Correct and distant with you; still brave, still stubborn.
secrets: He still keeps the hero’s road-map from Millbrook folded inside his gauntlet.
npcs.voice: Clipped and formal, colder than it used to be.

nodes.text: Ser Corwin stands among the Order's knights in a borrowed tabard. "You wished to speak to me?"

options.label: "I was wrong, Corwin. Ride with me again." (Persuasion DC 15)

advantageIf.source: Corwin heard how you calmed the crowd on the Ashfall road
Corwin heard you saved Millbrook's children first

success.text: Corwin looks at you for a long moment. Then he unpins the Order's badge from his cloak. "Once more, then. Do not make me regret it."

failure.text: "Words are cheap," says Corwin. "I have heard yours before."

options.label: "Ride with the Order, then. I will look for your banner in the fight."

outcome.text: Something eases in Corwin's face. "Look for it on the left," he says. "I will be there."

options.label: "Run back to your Order, then. It has always suited you better."

outcome.text: Corwin turns on his heel. The knights around him heard every word, and so, soon, will the whole Order.

nodes.text: Corwin falls in beside you as if he had never left.

npcs.name: Pyrraxis
npcs.personality: An ancient, proud red dragon, maddened for twenty-three years by the Tooth in her wound and the Choir’s song in her head. Under the hunger she is lucid, bitter and contemptuous of small things, and she remembers every knight who came for her.
secrets: She knows the lance that wounded her was poisoned with the Tooth, and she blames the Dawn Lance, not the Choir.
She would trade almost anything to be rid of the hunger.
npcs.voice: A voice like a furnace door: slow, amused, every word dropped from a great height. Calls the hero "small thing" or "little thief".

nodes.text: The great red head swings toward you, and the hoard shifts like a tide of coins. "Speak, small thing, before I remember I am hungry."

options.label: Speak past the hunger, to the dragon under it (Insight DC 16)

success.text: For a heartbeat her eyes clear. "Twenty-three years," she says, in a voice like a furnace door. "They sing in my blood, small thing. Make them stop." Then the hunger takes her back, but you know now that someone is still in there.

failure.text: There is nothing in her eyes but fire.

npcs.voice: Crisp and quick, a little too formal, with sudden flashes of dry humour.

success.text: Isolde laughs, the first laugh in the palace for a week, and has Hale count out three hundred gold from what is left of the treasury.

failure.text: The Queen's smile cools. "The treasury is ash, like half my city." The courtiers heard you ask.

options.label: "Rebuild Millbrook, Majesty. It stood for you when no one else did."

outcome.text: Isolde writes the order herself: timber, masons, and the Crown's tax on Millbrook forgiven for ten years.

options.label: "Spare Harrow Vey the rope, Majesty. Let him hang in the Isles, or not at all."

outcome.text: Isolde raises an eyebrow, but commutes the sentence to exile. Somewhere below, Harrow Vey is laughing.

endings.name: The Crown Endures
endings.text: Pyrraxis no longer threatens Aurelmark, the coup is broken, and Queen Isolde lives. The realm will march on the Gloamfen behind its Queen.

endings.name: The Regency Council
endings.text: The coup is broken and the dragon is gone, but the Queen is dead. A regency council rules in Highcrown while the Choir sings at the Maw.

endings.name: Crown in Ashes
endings.text: The palace is retaken, but Pyrraxis burned the upper tiers of Highcrown before she flew south to the Maw. The Choir has the Ember Tooth.

endings.name: Highcrown Fallen
endings.text: The Choir held the palace until it chose to leave. Highcrown is broken, and the Choir withdrew to the Maw untouched.
